benefits: Catches the small mistakes (a missing 512px icon, a typo in display) that silently break installability.
Checks icon sizes, colors, and enums against the real spec — not guesswork.
Runs instantly in your browser; no upload of your app's manifest to any server.
Clear pass/warn/fail verdicts tell you exactly what to fix and what is merely recommended.
Pairs with the Web App Manifest Generator to build, then verify, in one flow.

faqs.a: The installability bar: at minimum name (or short_name), start_url, display set to standalone/fullscreen/minimal-ui, and icons including 192px and 512px PNGs, served over HTTPS with a service worker. This checker verifies the manifest half of that list.

Android adaptive icons mask the icon into shapes (circle, squircle). A maskable icon includes safe padding so nothing important is cropped. Without one, Android may awkwardly crop your icon — hence the warning, not a failure.
faqs.q: Why does the checker want a maskable icon?

faqs.a: theme_color colors the browser toolbar and task switcher to match your brand; background_color is the splash-screen background shown while the app launches. Both should be valid CSS colors.
faqs.q: What are theme_color and background_color for?

faqs.a: Older manifests may omit id; modern browsers default it to start_url. An explicit id is recommended because changing start_url later would otherwise make the browser treat your app as a brand-new install, losing the old one.
faqs.q: Do I need the id field?

faqs.a: scope limits which URLs belong to your app — links outside it open in the browser instead. If omitted it defaults to the manifest's directory. Set it explicitly (usually "/") so navigation behaves predictably.

This checker validates the manifest document itself. For the full picture, also confirm the manifest is linked from your HTML (<link rel="manifest">), served with the right MIME type, over HTTPS, with a registered service worker — those are outside this tool's reach by design.
faqs.q: My manifest passes — is my PWA guaranteed installable?

pwa-manifest-checker.formula:
Installability checklist verified here:
1. name OR short_name present
2. start_url present
3. display in {fullscreen, standalone, minimal-ui, browser}
4. icons[] non-empty, with 192x192 and 512x512 entries
5. theme_color and background_color are valid CSS colors
6. Recommended: scope, id, description, maskable icon
Verdict: pass = required and valid, warn = recommended but missing, fail = required and missing/invalid.
howTo: Open your manifest file (usually manifest.webmanifest or manifest.json) and copy its full contents.
Paste the JSON into the box above. Validation runs instantly — nothing is uploaded.
Read the counts: passes, warnings, and failures.
Work through failures first — those block installability — then warnings.
Fix the issues in your manifest, paste again, and confirm everything passes.
keyFacts: A Web App Manifest is a JSON file that tells the browser your app's name, icons, colors, and how it should launch.
Browsers require specific fields before offering an install prompt: name/short_name, start_url, a valid display mode, and 192px + 512px icons.
The display field controls the app window: fullscreen, standalone (app-like, no browser UI), minimal-ui, or browser.
Icons should be PNG; a maskable purpose variant is recommended so Android adaptive icons don't crop your artwork.
theme_color tints the OS task switcher and browser UI; background_color fills the splash screen during launch.
The manifest must be linked from your HTML with <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest"> to take effect.
pwa-manifest-checker.keywords: pwa manifest checker, web app manifest validator, manifest.json checker, pwa installability test

labels.dBgFail: "{v}" is not a valid CSS color.
labels.dBgMissing: Missing — splash screen falls back to white.
labels.dDescWarn: Missing — recommended for install dialogs and app listings.
labels.dDisplayFail: "{v}" is not a valid display mode. Use fullscreen, standalone, minimal-ui, or browser.
labels.dDisplayMissing: Missing — browsers default to browser, which is not installable.
labels.dDisplayOk: "{v}" is a valid installable display mode.
labels.dIcon192Fail: No 192x192 icon found — required for installability.
labels.dIcon512Fail: No 512x512 icon found — required for installability.
labels.dIconsFail: The icons array is missing or empty.
labels.dIdWarn: Missing — id defaults to start_url; set it explicitly to survive URL changes.
labels.dMaskableWarn: No maskable icon — recommended so Android adaptive icons don't crop your artwork.
labels.dNameFail: Neither name nor short_name is present.
labels.dOrientationFail: "{v}" is not a valid orientation value.
labels.dScopeWarn: Missing — defaults to the manifest directory; set it explicitly (usually "/").
labels.dThemeFail: "{v}" is not a valid CSS color.
labels.dThemeMissing: Missing — browser UI falls back to default colors.
labels.emptyState: Paste your Web App Manifest JSON above to validate it.
labels.parseError: This is not valid JSON. Check for trailing commas, missing quotes, or truncated content.

limitations: Validates the manifest document only — not the <link rel="manifest"> tag, MIME type, HTTPS, or service worker.
Cannot fetch your icon files to confirm the sizes actually match the declared sizes.
Color validation uses the browser's CSS parser, so results can vary slightly by browser.
Very unusual but valid manifest extensions may be ignored by this checker.
